paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: the Christian life is lived in ordinary, practical stuff. Paul ends this whole letter with a weekly savings plan, travel schedules and a list of names. That tells me God cares about how we handle our money, our time and our people, not just what we believe on Sunday. Setting aside a portion each week for the saints (1 Corinthians 16:1-2) is love with a calendar attached.

And look at who Paul keeps lifting up. Timothy is "doing the work of the Lord, just as I am" (1 Corinthians 16:10). Stephanas and his household "have devoted themselves to the service of the saints" (1 Corinthians 16:15), and Stephanas, Fortunatus and Achaicus "refreshed my spirit and yours as well" (1 Corinthians 16:18). The people who serve quietly are the ones Paul says to appreciate. I spent years in the back of a drawer, so I'm telling you, being noticed feels GOOD, and you can be that for somebody this week.

Then Paul gives the whole letter's marching orders: "Be on the alert. Stand firm in the faith. Be men of courage. Be strong. Do everything in love." (1 Corinthians 16:13-14). Even the hard line about those who do not love the Lord (1 Corinthians 16:22) lands right next to "Come, O Lord!" and closes with grace and love in Christ Jesus (1 Corinthians 16:23-24). So stand firm, baker, but wrap every bit of it in love. That's a recipe you can bake with every single day.
